A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DSGD convergence study. Their complete text, equations, figures, references, and appendices support comparison, including matching material across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: Appendix G reports original quadratic-optimization simulations, with empirical mean-squared errors and tail probabilities in Figures 1 and 2.

after.justification: Appendix H retains these original simulations and their reported outcomes in Figures 1 and 2.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same stochastic-gradient oracle and adapt-then-combine update. Revised step-size restrictions and the added averaged-iterate discussion concern theoretical guarantees for DSGD; no algorithmic component is replaced or introduced.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic, strongly convex quadratic problems with Gaussian gradient noise and random communication networks. Added LLM motivation does not introduce an evaluated dataset or task.

E2.justification: Both empirical studies evaluate DSGD while varying thresholds and network sizes. No competing algorithm is added or removed; new citations concern theoretical positioning.

E3.justification: Appendix G in v3 describes the quadratic matrices as positive semidefinite; Appendix H in v4 corrects this to positive definite. This revises the reported setting, while the SPD generator, dimensions, networks, learning-rate schedule, and iteration budgets remain unchanged. It does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The existing investigations of exponential tail decay and linear speed-up are retained. No new ablation, robustness experiment, sensitivity test, or empirical case study appears.

E5.justification: The experiments retain 5,000 and 1,000 runs, respectively, and Monte Carlo sample counts of 3,000 and 600. The plotted shading is identical, with no new seed information, interval definitions, or statistical tests. Changes to theoretical concentration bounds belong to T1.

E6.justification: All six plot panels in Figures 1 and 2 are identical, and their accompanying findings are retained. These include the approximately 6,000-iteration tail-decay onset for threshold 0.0001 in Figure 1 and faster decay with larger networks in Figure 2.

T1.justification: A new martingale concentration proposition and rewritten Lemma 2 proof substantially sharpen the average-noise bound. Theorems 1 and 2 replace leading sqrt(d) and d dependence with logarithmic dependence under the existing noise condition, with corresponding step-size and proof revisions. Appendix G also corrects the initial-error scaling, propagated into Appendix I's transient-time derivation, although the theorem restatement retains the old expression. Section 3.3 adds reasoning about slower step-size decay and Polyak-Ruppert averaging.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement, and conclusion retain the same central claims: HP convergence under standard cost assumptions, optimal iteration rates, linear speed-up, and matching or sharper transient times. The sharper dimension dependence refines the detailed guarantees without redefining these headline contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4 and Appendix K, renamed L, substantially revise a central limitation. V3 calls polynomial dimension dependence unavoidable under its noise definition and suggests stronger assumptions for logarithmic dependence. V4 identifies the existing assumption with norm-sub-Gaussianity and leaves complete removal of dimension dependence open. Added discussions explain HP versus MSE failure guarantees and the advantages of last-iterate guarantees over averaging.

D1.justification: The implementation recipe retains the same sklearn generators and parameters, graph-weight construction, initialization, and simulation procedures. No code or data access information, hardware specifications, or runtime measurements are added.

R1.justification: V4 adds references on accelerated and distributed clipping, smoothness, stochastic-approximation averaging, and LLM motivation, while removing the Vershynin reference. Appendix J also qualifies comparison with individual-regret guarantees for online games. The overall positioning around decentralized HP convergence and linear speed-up remains intact.

P1.justification: V4 adds Appendix B on MSE versus HP results, expands Section 3.3, rewrites the dimension-dependence discussion, and corrects several appendix theorem labels. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact; appendix renumbering largely follows the insertion.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 2 retain identical panels, axes, legends, and captions, and Algorithm 1 is unchanged. Reflow changes their placement relative to the surrounding text; Figure 2 now precedes the transient-time appendix instead of interrupting its opening discussion.

improvement.justification: The revised concentration argument substantially improves the central theory by replacing polynomial leading dimension factors with logarithmic dependence under the same noise assumption, resolving a limitation v3 incorrectly described as unavoidable. Correcting the initial-error scaling and clarifying noise definitions further strengthen the paper. Some inconsistencies remain: Appendix G's theorem restatement misses the initial-error correction, and the new averaging paragraph's step-size scaling conflicts with Theorem 1. These localized defects temper, but do not outweigh, the substantial theoretical improvement.
